record.title: Stable element ids
record.requirement: every element of the stand carries a stable id: the author's key where given, else its component path
record.observed_gap: a node's id is a slot index plus a version; a remount re-clones nodes into fresh ids, and no semantic id exists — an agent can aim only at coordinates or selectors.

verification.acceptance: On each of the four lean stand tasks (counter, flight booker, timer, CRUD), booted by `seven_guis::stand` with `stand::options(false)` and `stand::options(true)`, `DioxusDocument::element_ids()` gives every element node of the document exactly one id, all pairwise distinct; an element whose HTML `id` is non-empty, `/`-free and the first of its value in document order reads that value verbatim (the TaskShell chrome and every lean-task control key), every other element reads its component path (the component names below the root, then `{tag}:{n}` / `{tag}[{key}]` element segments) or, outside every component (`html`, `head`, `body`), its document path `/html:0/…`; both layout modes read the same id list. Witness: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_element_ids` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_element_ids.rs).

record.notes:
2026-10-06 (2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits wrap): PREMISE CORRECTION, on the founder's ruling given at that chunk's phase (the founder, 2026-10-06; chunk inputs I1 · I2). This acceptance says every element that reads no author key "reads its component path … or, outside every component, … its document path". The id grammar now has a fourth tier between the author key and the component path: an unkeyed element under an element of its own component instance that reads an author key reads an anchored path, `{key}//{segment}` (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge). On the four lean tasks at boot no element reads an anchored path (178 ids over both layout modes, measured at that chunk), and CRUD's three rows, which read `TaskShell/Crud/div:0/div:1/div:0/div[{n}]` when this capability was verified, now read their author keys `crud-person-0` · `crud-person-1` · `crud-person-2`, each row carrying an HTML `id`. The outcome is unchanged: every element node reads exactly one id, all pairwise distinct, both layout modes equal. The witness is the same test file, green with its row pin re-spelled (`stand_element_ids`, 4 passed). Status, ref and acceptance text are left as written. Record: escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits/report.md.

2026-10-14 (2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep wrap): every driver screen of the four lean tasks reads one distinct id per node line, each an accessibility node's `author_id`, through `Session::run` alone, in both layout modes — tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_requirement_sweep.rs::every_requirement_holds_through_the_driver_on_every_lean_task (the plan's ledger-note entry; status, ref and acceptance untouched).

record.title: Id persistence
record.requirement: an element's id is identical across a re-render, a remount and a fresh process
record.observed_gap: a node's id is a slot index plus a version; a remount re-clones nodes into fresh ids, and no semantic id exists — an agent can aim only at coordinates or selectors.

verification.acceptance:
On each of the four lean stand tasks (counter, flight booker, timer, CRUD), in both layout modes (stand::options(false) and stand::options(true)), DioxusDocument::element_ids() reads the same id for each element across a re-render, a remount and a restart in a new process. Witness: cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_id_persistence.
- Re-render: after each task's scripted re-renders (counter increments; flight booker's return toggle and Book, which inserts #flight-booked; delivered timer ticks; CRUD filter, Delete and Create), every element node present before and after reads the same id, and the DOM verifiably changed. A CRUD person's row keeps its id under a filter, after another person's Delete, and after a Create.
- Remount: in seven_guis::app::app booted with stand::options, after the task's card → Back → the same card, the id list equals the pre-remount list in order. Every element's NodeId differs from its pre-remount NodeId, except the four document-skeleton elements DioxusDocument builds outside the VirtualDom (/html:0, /html:0/head:0, /html:0/body:0, main), which keep theirs; every dropped pre-remount NodeId reads None. The pre-remount list equals stand::boot's for that task.
- Fresh process: a child process with a pid distinct from the parent's re-executes the test binary and reads, for each task and mode, a non-empty id list equal to the parent's.

record.notes: 2026-10-06 PREMISE-CORRECTION (2026-10-06-id-persistence wrap): the Remount clause said "Every element's NodeId differs from its pre-remount NodeId, and every pre-remount NodeId reads None". That is false for the four document-skeleton elements (/html:0, /html:0/head:0, /html:0/body:0, main). DioxusDocument::new creates them outside the VirtualDom (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:104-129), so a task's remount never unmounts them: they keep their NodeId and still read their ids. Measured by stand_id_persistence::ids_hold_across_a_remount in both layout modes on the four lean tasks: the kept-NodeId set equals exactly those four; every other element's NodeId is fresh; every dropped pre-remount NodeId reads None. The clause is refined to name the exception; the outcome (the same id list in order across a remount, on fresh task nodes) is unchanged. Refined with evidence on the operator's decision at this wrap (operator, 2026-10-06). Evidence: escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-id-persistence/report.md (Spec claims disproved 2).

verification.acceptance: On the stand, in both layout modes, read through `DioxusDocument::snapshot` after real input: at boot `flight-one-way` reads `pressed: Some(true)` and `flight-return` `Some(false)`, the two readings swap after a click on `flight-return` and swap back after a click on `flight-one-way`, and no other node reads a `pressed`; with no row selected every CRUD row reads `selected: Some(false)`, after a click on a row exactly that row reads `Some(true)`, a click on another row moves the reading, and a filter edit or Delete leaves no row selected; `flight-start` reads `invalid: false` at boot and `true` once what it holds is no date, `flight-return-date` reads the same way under a return flight, and no other node reads invalid; each of these snapshot readings equals the accessibility node's (`is_selected`, `toggled`, `invalid`). Each reading follows the app's state when it changes, and through `escher_driver::Session::run` the step that changes it returns that node among its `changed` nodes as it reads after the step — the click on `flight-return` returns both mode buttons, a click on a row returns that row and the row it leaves, the `type` that makes `flight-start` no date returns it invalid and the `type` that makes it a date returns it not invalid — each returned diff equal to the check's own reading of the two snapshots and equal in both layout modes. Proved by `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_snapshot_state --test stand_act_diff` and `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test accessibility_states --test stand_act_states`, and by the same four files under `cargo test --workspace --locked --test accessibility_states --test stand_act_states --test stand_snapshot_state --test stand_act_diff`.
